chapter_title: Concerning the Five Saviours, the Resurrectors of Those Who Are Dead, Together with the Five Resurrections
chapter_note: This kephalaion is chiefly a pentadic, systematic enumeration of five “resurrectors/saviours” with cosmological agents (Father, Light Mind, etc.). The extant text is heavily lacunose at the start (first/second items partly lost) and ends with a generalized beatitude that reads like later exhortatory/pastoral closure rather than impersonal mechanism-teaching. The opening is a clear hagiographic dialogue frame.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic dialogue frame (“Once again the enlightener speaks”)—a compilation wrapper, not the substrate teaching.
Too fragmentary to date securely, but it appears to continue the broken opening frame/title line rather than giving a cosmological mapping or mechanism.
Enumerative, impersonal degree-structure (“second resurrector”) consistent with the pentadic teaching substrate; no institutional or citation markers.

paragraphs.core_text: And the third resurrector is the Father, the First [...], because by his word shall all lives [...] gather in and go to him, and they receive [...] and rest.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmological mechanism: resurrection effected “by his word,” lives gather and rest—cosmos→cosmos description without audience address or institutional pointing.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth resurrector is the Light Mind, because [...].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pentadic enumeration naming a cosmological being (“Light Mind”) in impersonal explanatory mode.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth resurrector to the good [...] is the Father, the First established one [...]. [He ...] all the powers, and he stands firm [...]. He shall unveil the [...] over them [...], and he draws them to him [...], his will [...], and he [...] them, and he stands them up [...] there, and they remain until [...].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Sustained cosmological process-description (unveiling, drawing, establishing, standing up powers) within the cosmic system; no institutional application language.

Beatitude-style address (“Blessed is every one…”) shifts from impersonal mechanism to generalized exhortatory blessing; functions as later devotional/pastoral closure rather than the enumerative substrate.
